newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS-up 3/8, await Anaheim, Calif.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS-up 3/8, await Anaheim, Calif.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices on Monday rose around three-eighths of a point, under the influence of stronger Treasuries, as the market looked ahead to a big sale on Tuesday by an Anaheim, Calif., authority.
The Anaheim Public Finance Authority plans to sell almost $458 million of revenue bonds to pay for public improvements that will help Walt Disney Co's theme park, Disneyland.
"It is the deal for the week," a trader said, noting that this week's calender was fairly slim.

The recent lack of new, California municipal bonds as well as views that retail demand in that state is fairly strong and the appeal of the Walt Disney Co all were cited as factors likely to create solid demand for the issue.
Traders noted that the deal also includes almost $59 million of taxable debt, so a variety of buyers were expected to be interested.
The Anaheim bond sale could help set the tone for the municipal market, which largely was driven by economic data and the rises achieved by the 30-year Treasury bond.
"We have nothing in the municipal market to give us any guidance at all," a municipal bond analyst said.
The market was looking ahead to a meeting by the Federal Reserve's policy-making arm on Tuesday, and crucial unemployment data that were slated for release on Friday.
Fixed-income markets, which are always wary of inflation, were soothed by the latest data on the manufacturing sector, which suggested a slowdown in the first quarter was likely.
The National Association of Purchasing Management's index read 52.0 percent in January, below the 53.0 level that was forecast, while supplier deliveries fell to 48.5 from 51.6 in December.
A reading above 50 is viewed by financial analysts as a sign of expansion, while a level below is considered to signal a contraction.
In the secondary market, Dade County Florida Water and Sewer System Revenues of October 2026, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.68 percent net, down three basis points.
And Houston, Texas, Water and Sewer System Revenues of December 2027, which have a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.76 percent, down two basis points.
March U.S. Treasury bond futures on the Chicago Board of Trade rose 28 ticks to 111-14/32, while the March municipal bond futures climbed 28 ticks to 115-8/32. The MOB spread stood at plus 122 ticks.

During the week of February 3, scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales were expected to total $1.56 billion in 66 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group. This total was down sharply from the $4 billion to $5 billion levels seen in December.
Competitive sales total $275 million in 42 sales. The largest is a $30 million Fresno Unified School District, Calif., offering on February 6.
Negotiated sales total $1.29 billion in 24 offerings.
